source.title: Learning Robust Recommender from Noisy Implicit Feedback
source.authors: Wen-Jie Wang; Fu-Li Feng; Xiang-Nan He; Li-Qiang Nie; Tat-seng Chua

record.file_problem: Text is the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests learning over time on noisy implicit-feedback interactions in recommender models, extending the real-patterns-before-noise idea to a different model and task setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training-loss results on true-positive and false-positive interactions. Its discussion of image-classification work and Arpit et al. is cited prior work, not a result from this study. No random-label image experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: Normal-training loss trajectories test V6 in neural recommendation: naturally noisy interactions are harder to fit early but are eventually fitted. This extends the learning-order question to implicit feedback.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: clean interactions are easier to fit early, normal training eventually fits false-positive interactions, and ADT reduces their influence. The paper's main conclusion also emphasizes improved recommendation quality and further gains from incorporating extra feedback.
record.recipe_differences: Uses recommender-model interaction-loss trajectories and noisy implicit feedback, rather than image classification with random labels; also compares denoising training interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The training method changes the false-positive loss trajectory: normal training eventually fits them, T-CE discards them, and R-CE slows fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: T-CE increases false-positive loss while overall loss falls; R-CE reduces false-positive loss more slowly while preserving a gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discarding or down-weighting hard interactions can prevent or slow their fitting in recommender training.

record.problems: The relevant trajectories are presented in figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The study tests naturally occurring false-positive interactions in recommender systems, not random labels in image networks.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result rows omitted.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption-fraction sweep, perfect training fit throughout, and test error approaching chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.

Artificially randomized labels and direct identification of shared representations or patterns. Evidence here concerns loss trajectories for naturally occurring false-positive feedback, identified through dwell-time or rating thresholds.

record.verdict_notes: Loss trajectories are reported graphically without uncertainty estimates. The ADT interventions do not warrant the record's limits_scope verdict on V6: they deliberately change which interactions receive optimization.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training and test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters are not tested.
Training time for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases are not tested.
Shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
A sweep from no corruption to all-random labels, perfect training fit, and test error are not tested.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their effects on random-label fitting or true-label generalization are not tested.

Tests true-positive versus naturally occurring false-positive interactions in recommender models, not random labels in standard image networks. It does not compare fully random labels or report training error.

rows.subject: NeuMF
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss over iterations for true-positive and false-positive interactions during normal training.
rows.measure: Training loss over iterations; false-positive interaction loss is clearly larger in early stages, and both losses converge to close values later.
rows.note: The text describes false-positive interactions as harder to memorize early and says the losses later converge to close values, indicating that NeuMF eventually fits both.
rows.check: No substantive correction. Figure 2 compares true-positive and false-positive losses directly; their later similarity indicates fitting, not demonstrated zero training error.

rows.subject: GMF
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss over iterations for false-positive interactions and all training interactions during normal training.
rows.measure: CE loss over iterations; false-positive interaction loss eventually becomes similar to the loss of other interactions.
rows.locator: Section 5.2, Figure 8(a) and discussion on page 9
rows.note: The text says this indicates GMF eventually fits false-positive interactions well.
rows.check: The comparator is all training interactions, not a separate clean-only group. Section 5.2 begins on page 8; Figure 8 is on page 9. The result is qualitative and does not establish zero training error.

rows.subject: GMF+T-CE
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss over iterations for false-positive interactions and all training interactions with Truncated Loss.
rows.measure: CE loss over iterations; false-positive interaction loss increases while overall training loss decreases.
rows.locator: Section 5.2, Figure 8(b) and discussion on page 9
rows.note: The text says parameters are not optimized over these interactions, so T-CE discards them rather than eventually memorizing them.
rows.check: This is a denoising intervention that deliberately removes large-loss interactions from optimization. Its prevention of later memorization is method behavior, not evidence against the normal-training learning sequence in V6. The reported loss increase is supported by the supplied text.

rows.subject: GMF+R-CE
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss over iterations for false-positive interactions and all training interactions with Reweighted Loss.
rows.measure: CE loss over iterations; false-positive interaction loss decreases, but remains larger than real training loss.
rows.locator: Section 5.2, Figure 8(c) and discussion on page 9
rows.note: The text says the model still fits false-positive interactions, though their larger loss values indicate that reweighting prevents it from fitting them quickly.
rows.check: Deliberately down-weighting hard interactions changes their learning trajectory. The remaining loss gap measures the denoising method's effect and does not independently establish or contradict the clean-first sequence in V6.

relationships.condition: Normal training: NeuMF on Adressa and GMF on Amazon-book.
relationships.reason: R1 shows higher noisy-interaction loss early and similar clean/noisy losses later; R2 shows eventual convergence of noisy-interaction loss toward the aggregate training loss.
relationships.display_finding: Noisy-interaction losses were higher early, later approached clean-interaction losses, and eventually converged toward aggregate training loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NeuMF on Adressa and GMF under normal training on Amazon-book
reader_labels.reason: False-positive interaction loss is larger early, then converges toward other interaction loss later, consistent with learning true patterns earlier and eventually fitting noisy interactions (R1, R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: With T-CE, false-positive interactions are discarded; with R-CE, their loss decreases but remains higher, so the later learning pattern depends on the training method (R3, R4).
